title: Resource
text: Abstract (Resource) The Rat Resource and Research Center (RRRC) provides a unique and essential repository service to the research community by importing, storing and distributing a large number of rat strains and embryonic stem cell lines. It assures that valuable models are preserved and made available to interested investigators, allows researchers to satisfy NIH requirements for resource sharing, relieves individual investigators from the burden of animal distribution and ensures that models are maintained with rigorous genetic quality control and health monitoring standards to enhance experimental reproducibility. Our objective during the next funding period is to continue to improve and expand the functions and capabilities of the RRRC to provide biomedical investigators with the rat models, embryonic stem cells, related reagents, protocols and services that will facilitate their research. We will accomplish this by developing new and utilizing existing technologies to improve the quality of the resource’s acquisition, cryopreservation, storage, quality control, and distribution of rats, sperm, embryos and embryonic stem cells. We will continue to evaluate and improve our service delivery and our communication with the biomedical research community. We will expand our services which already include re-derivation, colony management, a wide array of genetic analysis options, model creation using CRISPR/Cas9 technology, and microbiota characterization on a fee-for-service basis. In this way, the RRRC will strengthen its ability to serve as a much-needed “one stop” resource for investigators using rats in biomedical research.

title: Medical Genetics Research Fellowship Program
text:
This grant supports research training for primarily MD & MD/PhD, and secondarily PhD trainees enrolled in the
Department of Molecular and Human Genetics ABMGG residency and fellowship programs at Baylor College
of Medicine. It has a long tradition of training current and future leaders in medical genetics research.

title: Exploring RNA Polymerase Dynamics and Regulatory Architecture Across Divergent Bacterial Species
text:
Bacterial RNAP is a proven and attractive antibiotic target. Many of the bacterial species we study
cause human disease, making their transcription mechanisms directly relevant to human health.
Understanding how RNAP controls gene expression will not only advance basic biology but also
inform strategies to promote human health.

title: Molecular and Cellular Regulation of Pre-Leukemic Stem Cells and their Therapeutic Targeting
text:
Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS) and Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) are paradigmatic cancers of the blood
system that have dismal clinical outcome and cure rates have not improved in 50 years for the majority of
patients. Research has shown the existence and critical role of pre-leukemic stem cells (preL-SC) and their
subclonal complexity in MDS and AML pathogenesis, progression, and therapeutic resistance. The proposed
research will study preL-SC subclonal complexity in patient samples and murine models, identify mechanisms
of transcriptional dysregulation governing preL-SC, and test novel pharmacological approaches directly targeting
preL-SC-relevant mechanisms in MDS, AML, and related pre-malignant conditions.

title: The Role of Food Sensitization in Cardiovascular Disease
text:
Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death in the United States and worldwide.
Using the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, this project evaluates the novel hypothesis that
the presence of food specific IgE (sensitization), a prevalent condition, is a risk factor for
cardiovascular disease, and that consumption of the food allergen modifies this risk.
Establishing food sensitization as a risk factor for cardiovascular disease would provide new
opportunities for prevention and could have major implications for how food allergy is managed.

title: Active and passive humoral immunity to enteric adenovirus infection in Bangladeshi children
text:
As diarrheal disease is consistently a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children under 5 worldwide
and adenovirus (AdV) 40/41 identified as a leading cause, there is a great need for further study of this
pathogen, particularly the immune response to infection. Successful completion of the proposed aims will serve
as the perfect vehicle for development into an independent translational investigator, provide invaluable insight
into the humoral response to adenovirus (AdV) 40/41 infection using a cohort in Bangladesh and bring us one
step closer in discovering immune targets for vaccine development.

title: Identifying Cell Type-Specific RNA Expression and Regulatory Changes in Entorhinal Cortex Clinical Samples of Alzheimer's Disease
text:
CLIP-FANS provides for the first time, an approach that can identify cell-type specific RBP mediated RNA
regulation in human clinical samples. Alzheimer’s disease is one neurodegenerative disease that has cell
selective vulnerability and dysregulation of RBPs. CLIP-FANS and FANSseq will identify the cell-type specific
gene expression and regulatory changes in AD to identify disease-specific differences for potential therapeutic
targets.

title: Community-Engaged Approach to Supporting South Asians w/ Type 2 Diabetes at Risk for Depression
text:
T2D is high among South Asian Americans, and available data indicate that depression is high but mental
health service utilization is low in this population. Building on an innovative and successful community health
worker (CHW)-led T2D intervention (DREAM Initiative - R01DK11048), this K01 proposal will adapt this CHW-
led T2D intervention to include mental health and digital health components, and test the feasibility and
acceptability of this intervention to support South Asians with T2D who are at risk for depression. Findings from
this pilot study will inform a future randomized controlled trial to assess for scalability and efficacy.

title: Pharmacodynamically directed targeted therapy for leukemia
text:
Potent targeting of pyrimidine synthesis by DHODH inhibition represents a vulnerability to acute myeloid
leukemia (AML) and enhances decitabine efficacy in TP53 mutated AML. This proposal seeks to translate this
effort with a potent DHODHi (HOSU-53) utilizing a novel clinical trial design, detailed pharmacokinetics,
pharmacodynamics and intra-tumor response assessment with single cell DNA sequencing to monitor for clone
elimination in patients with AML followed by a combination trial with HOSU-53 + decitabine in TP53 mutated
AML.

title: Center for Neurovascular Engineering Research and adVanced Education (NERVE)
text: NERVE, a pioneering biomedical engineering center, aims to advance mini-brain technology and drug delivery system through cutting-edge research, imaging and animal testing capacity building, PhD program establishment, and the cultivation of a next generation workforce, transforming the field for the next generation.

title: Enhancing Biomedical Engineering, Imaging, and Technology Acceleration (BEITA) at North Carolina Central University
text:
Our program builds upon the strengths of North Carolina Central University (NCCU), a top Historically
Black College or University in the heart of Durham, NC, adjacent to world-class institutions and a
booming biotechnology hub. The program will build research capacity centered on bioprinting and
imaging approaches, with applications in many fields, including tissue engineering, materials science,
pharmaceutical development, and drug validation. The outcomes will provide experiential learning
opportunity, an enriched curriculum at both undergraduate and graduate level and bridge NCCU
trainees to biomedical engineering, imaging, and technology acceleration fields.

title: PNPLA3 in Susceptibility and Resistance to Fatty Liver Disease
text:
Fatty liver disease (FLD) is a burgeoning health problem with few therapeutic options. We have
used human genetics to identify genetic variants in a gene called PNPLA3. One variant confers
increased susceptibility and the other increased resistance to FLD. In this application we will build
on these discoveries to glean new insights into the pathogenesis of FLD with a goal of developing
new strategies and targets for the treatment of chronic liver disease.

title: Genetics of Cocaine Sensitivity in Drosophila
text:
HEALTH RELEVANCE
Illegal use of psychostimulants such as cocaine presents a worldwide health problem with huge socioeconomic
costs to societies; however, little is known about genetic risk factors for substance abuse. We will use the
powerful Drosophila melanogaster genetic model to precisely map variants that affect cocaine preference and
consumption, perform a systems genetic analysis to infer causal regulatory networks associated with these
traits, and use germline gene editing to prove causality of the genetic associations with cocaine preference and
gene regulatory networks. Since approximately 67% of Drosophila genes have a human counterpart, both
general principles derived from these studies and individual network elements will be relevant to human
substance abuse phenotypes.

title: Estrogenic regulation of the hippocampal ubiquitin-proteasome system and its role in memory and structural plastcity
text:
Memory impairments are characteristic of many neurological disorders, yet the development of effective treat-
ments to reduce these deficits is hampered by our relatively rudimentary knowledge about the neural mecha-
nisms through which memories are formed in males and females. The proposed research is relevant to public
health because it will fundamentally advance our understanding of the neural mechanisms underlying hormo-
nal regulation of memory formation in males and females, which will provide sorely needed insights that could
lead to the generation of novel therapies specifically tailored to reduce memory dysfunction in patients of each
sex. As such, the proposed research is particularly relevant to the mission of NINDS to use fundamental
knowledge about the brain and nervous system to reduce the burden of neurological disease for all people.

title: Acquisition of a Highly Sensitive Time of Flight (ToF) Mass Spectrometry System with Novel Fragmentation Capabilities for Qualitative and Quantitative Analysis
text:
Successful acquisition of a high speed and high sensitivity Sciex ZenoTOF 7600+ mass spectrometer will have
significant and broad impact on a wide array of biomedical research projects conducted on the health sciences
campus at the University of Wisconsin (UW)-Madison. This cutting-edge instrument will provide advanced mass
spectrometric capabilities that facilitate deciphering molecular details in a broad spectrum of projects in our user
group. The proposed instrument will support 23 major and minor users with 66 funded federal grants or contracts
and will accelerate the pace of ongoing research in many departments, colleges and campus units at UW.
Additionally, it will be available to the broader scientific community in Madison, the State of Wisconsin, and
beyond.

title: Mobilize Center: Models for Mobile Sensing and Precision Rehabilitation
text:
Limited mobility due to conditions like osteoarthritis, neuromuscular disease, and limb loss affects millions of
people, at a great cost to public health and personal well-being. The Mobilize Center is creating critically
needed tools to enable researchers to rapidly measure and analyze movement to uncover the factors that limit
mobility and predict the effects of treatments. The Mobilize Center, together with the thousands of researchers
we support, aims to revolutionize how we diagnose, monitor, and treat mobility limitations and enable
personalized rehabilitation at low cost and on a large scale using mobile sensing technology.

title: Developing next-generation high-content image-based genetic screens for multi-omic spatial phenotypes
text:
The spatial organization of DNA and RNA in our cells regulate important genomic functions such as gene
expression and localized protein production in specific sub-cellular regions, and the spatial organization of
DNA and RNA is regulated in turn by upstream regulatory mechanisms. Yet our understanding of what
regulators control the spatial organization of DNA and RNA is far from complete, due to a lack of large-scale
discovery technologies. This study will invent a new technology platform that will enable highly efficient
discovery of upstream regulators of the DNA and RNA organization, which will help elucidate and engineer the
spatial axis of molecular biology in health and disease.

title: Mechanisms of paclitaxel sensitivity and resistance
text:
Only ~50% of patients benefit from the commonly used chemotherapy drug paclitaxel, but it has not been
possible to predict which patients will respond. This project builds on preliminary evidence that pre-existing
chromosomal instability (CIN) is a key determinant of paclitaxel response. Through clinical evaluation of this
hypothesis, state-of-the-art measures of CIN, and consideration of an important modifier we recently identified
called pole focusing, this project will provide the basic knowledge required to develop a predictive biomarker
for paclitaxel and identify novel drug targets for sensitizing paclitaxel-resistant cancers.

title: Protein and Structural Core
text: The Protein/Structure Core (Core 1) is poised to offer strong support for the work outlined in Projects 2 and 4. Core 1 has two major tasks. Task 1 involves developing a novel affinity purification system using strong peptide-protein interactions. This system aims to generate a substantial quantity of high-quality STING protein for comprehensive cryo-EM and mass spectrometry analyses. In Task 2, we will establish the most advanced pipeline for single-particle cryo-EM structural determination. Firstly, we will develop an innovative supporting film for the cryo-EM grid, protecting the integrity of the STING protein during grid handling. Subsequently, we will identify nanobodies with strong affinity for STING, enhancing particle alignment in cryo-EM studies. Lastly, we will apply recent instrumental advancements in cryo-EM to capture the highest quality cryo-EM images. The integration of these technological advances facilitated by Core 1 will enable the cryo-EM determination of the STING/antagonist complex to near-atomic resolution.

title: Understanding the Impact of Micro- and Nanoplastics on Preterm Birth
text:
This research will provide the first comprehensive understanding of how specific types of microplastic particles
accumulate in the placenta during pregnancy and potentially contribute to preterm birth, which affects 15 million
infants annually worldwide. By revealing how these common environmental contaminants impact pregnancy,
this study will identify opportunities to reduce harmful exposures and protect maternal-child health. The findings
will offer actionable insights to guide future efforts to mitigate risks from microplastic exposure during pregnancy.
